title: The Tiamat pile: five dragons against a telegraphed board wipe

board.you: Turn 8, Tiamat just resolved (cast, so the search trigger is on the stack). Battlefield: Tiamat, Temur Ascendancy, Garruk's Uprising, six lands. Life 31.
board.table: Player 2 (the known sweeper deck — Esper) has SEVEN lands untapped after passing with mana up two turns running; everyone at the table reads Supreme-Verdict-shaped mana. Player 3 and 4 have small boards and are visibly waiting for Player 2 to act.

scenario.question: Tiamat's trigger searches for up to five differently-named Dragon cards to HAND — the pile is yours to design. Against telegraphed sweeper mana: do you fetch the all-gas pile (Terror of the Peaks, Scourge of Valkas, Lathliss, Miirym, Atarka) and commit next turn, fetch a resilience pile built around haste + protection pieces you can deploy across two turns, or fetch value-recursion (Haven of the Spirit Dragon is on-board fetchable? — no, it's a land — design around what the deck actually offers: which five names, and why)? Name the exact five cards and the sequencing plan.

branches.choice: All-gas pile — Terror of the Peaks, Scourge of Valkas, Lathliss, Miirym, Drakuseth — and commit next turn
branches.line: Fetch the five biggest payoffs still in the library — one correction to the question's suggested pile: Atarka, World Render is not in this deck, and Drakuseth, Maw of Flames is the top-end burn body. Next turn, deploy as many as seven lands allow — with eminence that is Terror ({2}{R}{R}) plus Scourge of Valkas ({1}{R}{R}{R}), both hasty via Temur Ascendancy — and attack, holding the rest for the turn after.
branches.signals: The table watched Tiamat fetch five, then watched you slam two payoffs into seven untapped Esper lands. Player 2 does not need to read tells; the Verdict timing is now scripted for them.
branches.coalition_risk: Maximal. You become the archenemy on the exact turn the sweeper deck is best positioned, and Players 3 and 4 — visibly waiting for Player 2 to act — will happily let the wrath resolve.
branches.coaching: The math fails before the politics do. Six lands plus a drop means roughly two Dragons per turn even with eminence. You cannot deploy enough of this pile to kill Player 2 through seven mana of held interaction before the sweep — so the wrath eats Tiamat plus your two best payoffs while three uncastable dragons watch from your hand. That is the textbook wrath-math violation (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math): commit exactly what wins before the wrath, and nothing here wins before it. One temptation to name and refuse: slotting Wrathful Red Dragon into this pile as sweeper insurance. Stack 004's verified 39-damage redirect fires on DAMAGE dealt to your Dragons — Blasphemous Act mana. Supreme-Verdict-shaped mana is a destroy effect; it triggers Wrathful zero times, and a can't-be-countered wrath ignores your permission too. The all-gas pile is the right fetch at a tapped-out table; it is the wrong fetch into telegraphed mana.

branches.choice: Staggered pile — Hellkite Courser, Goldspan Dragon, Miirym, Old Gnawbone, Lathliss — played in two waves
branches.line: Fetch pieces that either ignore the sweeper or rebuild through it. Wave one (next turn): Goldspan Dragon ({2}{R}{R} after eminence), attack Player 2 with Goldspan and Tiamat — both hasty via Ascendancy — pressuring the Esper life total and forcing the Verdict onto a two-body board; the attack banks a Treasure that survives the wipe. Wave two (post-wrath): Hellkite Courser ({3}{R}{R} after eminence) puts The Ur-Dragon onto the battlefield from the command zone with haste; attack with both, the commander trigger draws two and deploys a fetched Dragon free from hand, then the commander returns to the command zone at end step — untouchable, untaxed, having never been cast. Then Old Gnawbone and Lathliss unload: Gnawbone connections bank Treasures toward the deck's verified kill line, and Lathliss rebuilds width with every Dragon after.
branches.signals: Wave one reads as pressure, not commitment — two attackers against a control deck is what the whole table wants from you. The scary names stay hidden in hand, where the sweeper cannot price them.
branches.coalition_risk: Medium and managed. You take the archenemy mantle only after the table's one near-certain reset has been spent, and the Courser turn ends with the commander safely back in the zone.
branches.coaching: The point of designing a Tiamat pile into sweeper mana is fetching cards the sweeper cannot tax. Treasures are artifacts. Your draw-and-haste layer (Temur Ascendancy, Garruk's Uprising) is enchantments. And a Courser-loaned commander is a rental: even if Player 2 wipes in response to the Courser trigger, the commander goes to the graveyard and the state-based action returns him to the command zone, with no tax accrued — the tax counts only casts from the command zone, which this never was (Courser is the deck's real commander cheat; verified stack 005 refuted the Sneak Attack route). Old Gnawbone earns the fifth seat over another pure payoff: he is half of the verified table-kill — Gnawbone plus Aggravated Assault kills sequentially at net +2 Treasures per cycle (stack 006) — and Assault is an enchantment the Verdict never touches, so if you draw or Enlightened-Tutor into it post-wrath, this pile converts straight into the kill. Fund the activations with Gnawbone's Treasures: deck-facts flags five of your mana sources as spells-only, and none of that mana can ever pay Assault's {3}{R}{R}. You lose Tiamat and Goldspan to the wipe; that is the price of forcing it on a board you chose. Goldfish note: protection is in hand by turn 6 in 66.0% of games — if you are actually holding Teferi's Protection or Heroic Intervention here, you can shift weight toward Branch A's speed. Design the pile for the third of games you are not.

citations.quote: If a commander is in a graveyard or in exile and that object was put into that zone since the last time state-based actions were checked, its owner may put it into the command zone.
A commander cast from the command zone costs an additional {2} for each previous time the player casting it has cast it from the command zone that game.

branches.choice: Fetch gas but deploy nothing until the sweeper resolves
branches.line: Fetch any five (the Branch B names are fine), then pass with mana up for turns, deploying zero Dragons until Player 2 is forced to spend the wrath on Players 3 and 4 — or until they tap out for something else.
branches.signals: Total passivity from the Dragon deck after a five-card Tiamat fetch fools nobody. The table knows your hand is loaded, and Player 2 knows the Verdict is live against you whenever you finally move.
branches.coalition_risk: Low now, worst-case later: Players 3 and 4 have small boards, so Player 2 may simply never be forced to sweep — and every stand-off turn, their seven lands also fund counters and draw while your three free draw steps rotate to all three opponents.
branches.coaching: The stand-off math runs against you. Tiamat dies to the sweep whenever it comes, board or no board, so holding back protects almost nothing you have not already committed — while Branch B's Goldspan probe pressures the Esper life total and banks sweep-proof Treasure at the cost of one fetched card. The one honest argument for waiting — drawing into Aggravated Assault or Sneak Attack, the enchantments that turn a post-wrath hand into a verified kill (stacks 006, 005) — is an argument Branch B already banks: those draws arrive on the same schedule whether you probe or not, and the probe adds Treasures that will legally fund Assault where your spells-only sources cannot (deck-facts). Passive turns are free draw steps for the table (strategy:pivot-point), and against a draw-go deck specifically, time is their axis, not yours. Force the wrath on a board you designed to lose cheaply; do not wait for a tap-out that a competent control player will never volunteer.

recommendation.choice: Staggered pile — Hellkite Courser, Goldspan Dragon, Miirym, Old Gnawbone, Lathliss — played in two waves
recommendation.rationale: Into seven lands of telegraphed Verdict mana, the winning pile is the one that makes the sweeper hit air. Force the wipe with a cheap two-attacker probe, keep the multipliers in hand, then rent the commander through Hellkite Courser — the deck's verified commander cheat (stack 005) — for a draw-two-plus-free-Dragon turn that ends with him back in the command zone, untaxed (903.8's tax counts casts, and 903.9a covers him even if he dies mid-loan). Your enchantment layer survives the wrath, so wave two arrives hasty and drawing, and the fetched Old Gnawbone stands one Aggravated Assault draw away from the verified sequential table-kill (stack 006), funded by Treasures the Verdict cannot touch. Branch A commits into the wrath's best turn — and its Wrathful-insurance instinct fails against a destroy effect. Branch C waits for a tap-out that never comes (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math, strategy:pivot-point).
